questions.scenario: It is 1519, and as a prince-elector of the Holy Roman Empire you must choose the next emperor. The young Habsburg King Charles I of Spain and King Francis I of France both court your vote with promises and gold.
questions.prompt: Which candidate did the electors ultimately choose, crowned emperor in 1520?
questions.butterflyEffect: Charles V's election united Habsburg Spain, Austria, and the Holy Roman Empire under one ruler, forming a vast transcontinental power without precedent in Europe. His reign brought decades of rivalry with France and coincided with the eruption of Martin Luther's Reformation, which Charles spent much of his rule trying to contain.

choices.text: Charles V of the House of Habsburg
Francis I of France
Henry VIII of England
Frederick the Wise of Saxony

questions.scenario: You are a passenger aboard Indian Airlines Flight 814, hijacked shortly after takeoff from Kathmandu on Christmas Eve 1999. The plane has been forced to land in Taliban-controlled Kandahar, and the hijackers are demanding the release of imprisoned militants.
questions.prompt: What did the Indian government ultimately do to end the week-long hijacking crisis?
questions.butterflyEffect: India released militants Masood Azhar, Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh, and Mushtaq Ahmed Zargar in exchange for the 176 hostages. Azhar went on to found Jaish-e-Mohammed, later responsible for major attacks in India, while Sheikh was convicted in the 2002 kidnapping and murder of journalist Daniel Pearl.

choices.text: Released Masood Azhar and two other militants in exchange for the hostages
Launched a special forces raid on the aircraft
Refused all demands, leading to a prolonged siege
Paid a cash ransom while refusing to free any prisoners

questions.scenario: You are the captain of an Embraer E190 on approach to Grozny on 25 December 2024 when a shockwave tears through the fuselage, shredding your hydraulic lines and controls.
questions.prompt: What did the crew do to try to save the crippled aircraft and its passengers?
questions.butterflyEffect: The pilots fought to keep the jet airborne across nearly 300 miles of the Caspian Sea before losing control on approach to Aktau, killing 38 of the 67 aboard. Investigators pointed to a Russian air-defense missile fired amid a drone alert, and Russia's president later apologized for the incident occurring in Russian airspace, straining ties with Azerbaijan.

choices.text: Attempted to divert the damaged jet across the Caspian Sea toward Aktau
Immediately ditched the aircraft in the sea near Grozny
Turned back to Baku using a backup hydraulic system
Requested an emergency landing at the nearest Russian military airbase

questions.scenario: You are a passenger on Northwest Flight 253 nearing Detroit on Christmas Day 2009, and you notice the man in seat 19A fumbling with something under a blanket moments before flames erupt.
questions.prompt: What stopped Abdulmutallab from detonating the explosive sewn into his underwear?
questions.butterflyEffect: Nearby passengers and a flight attendant tackled Abdulmutallab and smothered the flames before serious damage occurred; he suffered burns but the plane landed safely. The failed attack exposed watch-list failures and led to the rapid nationwide rollout of full-body airport security scanners.

choices.text: Passengers and crew tackled him and put out the fire
Air marshals shot him before he could act
The device simply failed to ignite on its own
The pilot depressurized the cabin, extinguishing the flames

questions.scenario: You are aboard a Russian Defence Ministry Tu-154 lifting off from Sochi on Christmas Day 2016, carrying the Alexandrov Ensemble toward a New Year's concert for troops deployed in Syria.
questions.prompt: What happened to the aircraft moments after it climbed away from Sochi?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Tu-154 plunged into the Black Sea minutes after takeoff, killing all 92 aboard, including nearly the entire Alexandrov Ensemble choir and humanitarian doctor Elizaveta Glinka. Investigators attributed the crash to pilot error and disorientation in darkness, dealing a severe blow to Russia's military cultural corps and hastening the aging Tu-154's retirement from state service.

choices.text: It stalled and crashed into the Black Sea, killing everyone aboard
It suffered engine failure and made a safe emergency landing
It was struck by a missile and diverted to Turkey
It caught fire on the runway before departure

questions.scenario: It is October 1999. Maurice Papon, convicted the year before of crimes against humanity for his role in deporting Jews from Bordeaux, has fled to Switzerland rather than serve his ten-year sentence.
questions.prompt: What actually happens to Papon as French authorities pursue him abroad?
questions.butterflyEffect: Swiss police arrested Papon and he was extradited back to France, where he was imprisoned to serve his sentence. Ill health saw him released in 2002, and his 1998 trial remains one of the most significant reckonings with France's Vichy-era collaboration in Wold War II.

choices.text: He is arrested in Switzerland and extradited to France to serve his sentence
Switzerland grants him political asylum and he lives there freely
He escapes to Argentina and evades capture for the rest of his life
French courts overturn his conviction on appeal before he can be caught

questions.scenario: It is October 22, 2008, at India's Satish Dhawan Space Centre. You watch the PSLV rocket carrying Chandrayaan-1, India's first lunar probe, climb into the sky, its instruments destined to scan the Moon's surface from orbit.
questions.prompt: What major discovery does Chandrayaan-1's instrument later make about the Moon?
questions.butterflyEffect: Chandrayaan-1's Moon Mineralogy Mapper detected evidence of water molecules bound in the lunar soil, a finding that reshaped assumptions about the Moon's dryness. The mission's success helped launch India's broader lunar program, leading directly to the Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 missions.

choices.text: Evidence of water molecules in the lunar soil
Proof that the Moon has a thin breathable atmosphere
Discovery of a previously unknown ocean of liquid rock
Confirmation that the Moon is hollow

questions.scenario: It is October 22, 2005, and forecasters have just run out of the year's pre-assigned storm names. A new tropical depression over the eastern Caribbean is designated Tropical Storm Alpha, the first Atlantic storm ever named from the Greek alphabet, and it is bearing down on an already storm-battered Hispaniola.
questions.prompt: What actually follows as Alpha moves over Haiti and the Dominican Republic?
questions.butterflyEffect: Alpha's heavy rain triggered severe flooding and mudslides across Haiti and the Dominican Republic, adding to a brutal, record-breaking hurricane season. The exhaustion of the naming list was so unusual it happened only once more, in 2020, prompting meteorologists to later retire the Greek-letter system altogether.

choices.text: It causes deadly flooding and mudslides on Hispaniola
It dissipates over open ocean without reaching land
It strengthens into a major hurricane and strikes Florida
It merges harmlessly with Hurricane Wilma far offshore

questions.scenario: It is October 22, 1983, and two correctional officers have just been killed by inmates within hours of each other inside the United States Penitentiary at Marion, Illinois. As warden, you must decide how to respond immediately.
questions.prompt: What response follows the killings at USP Marion?
questions.butterflyEffect: Marion was placed under an indefinite total lockdown, confining prisoners to their cells for nearly all hours with severely restricted contact. The "Marion Lockdown" became the model for the modern American supermax prison, most notably ADX Florence, and fueled decades of debate over long-term solitary confinement.

choices.text: The prison is placed under an indefinite, total lockdown
The prison is closed and all inmates transferred elsewhere permanently
Guards are withdrawn and inmates granted self-governance
Congress immediately abolishes the federal penitentiary system

questions.scenario: It is October 1964. Ian Fleming died two months ago, but the publisher is now releasing his children's novel Chitty-Chitty-Bang-Bang, inspired by a real 1920s racing car and the bedtime stories Fleming told his young son.
questions.prompt: What actually happens to Chitty-Chitty-Bang-Bang in the years after publication?
questions.butterflyEffect: The story was adapted into the beloved 1968 musical film Chitty Chitty Bang Bang starring Dick Van Dyke, which later inspired a stage musical as well. It became one of Fleming's most enduring legacies outside the Bond series, reaching generations of children who never read a spy novel.

choices.text: It is adapted into a hit 1968 musical film
It is banned in Britain for its content
It is quickly forgotten and never reprinted
It is immediately staged as a Broadway play

questions.scenario: It's March 1997 in Wollaston, Northamptonshire. Gravel-mining machinery is due on site any day, and your excavation team has just uncovered a corroded iron mass inside a young warrior's grave.
questions.prompt: What is the right way to handle the fragile iron mass before the miners arrive?
questions.butterflyEffect: The corroded mass was carefully block-lifted and taken to conservators, who painstakingly revealed a complete boar-crested Anglo-Saxon helmet. It proved to be only the sixth such helmet ever found in Britain, now displayed as a centerpiece of Northamptonshire's archaeological heritage.

choices.text: Have specialists lift it intact in a soil block for lab conservation
Scrub the corrosion off with a wire brush to see what's inside
Leave it in place and let the mining proceed around it
Quietly sell the find to a private antiquities collector

questions.scenario: It's December 23, 2008, hours after President Lansana Conté's death ends his 24-year rule. You are Captain Moussa Dadis Camara, watching Guinea's constitutional succession process unfold with no army backing it yet.
questions.prompt: What do you do to seize control of the country before civilian succession takes hold?
questions.butterflyEffect: Camara's junta, the National Council for Democracy and Development, ruled Guinea by force for nearly two years, a period marred by a 2009 massacre of opposition demonstrators. After Camara was wounded in an assassination attempt, he stepped aside, and Alpha Condé's 2010 election victory finally restored civilian government.

choices.text: Announce a military junta and suspend the constitution
Allow the National Assembly speaker to assume the interim presidency as written
Call for an immediate election within days under existing law
Defer entirely to the army chief of staff's authority

questions.scenario: It's December 23, 1783, in the Maryland State House at Annapolis. The Revolutionary War is won, and you, General Washington, stand before the Confederation Congress still holding supreme command of the Continental Army.
questions.prompt: What do you do with the military authority you have held for eight years of war?
questions.butterflyEffect: Washington voluntarily resigned his commission and returned to private life at Mount Vernon, stunning contemporaries including King George III, who reportedly called it the noblest act of his life. The precedent of a victorious general surrendering power set the template for civilian control that Washington reaffirmed when he later left the presidency after two terms.

choices.text: Formally resign your commission and return power to Congress
Retain command until the new government is fully established
Accept the informal suggestions that you become king
March the army on Congress to secure soldiers' unpaid wages first

questions.scenario: It's December 23, 2007, in Kathmandu. Nepal's interim parliament, seeking to end a decade of civil war and the king's discredited rule, debates the fate of the 240-year-old monarchy.
questions.prompt: What does the interim parliament agree Nepal should become?
questions.butterflyEffect: The agreement paved the way for the monarchy's formal abolition in May 2008, when the newly elected Constituent Assembly declared Nepal a federal democratic republic. It ended the Shah dynasty's 240-year reign, though the country's fragile coalition politics and the peace process with former Maoist rebels continued to unfold for years afterward.

choices.text: A federal democratic republic, abolishing the monarchy
A constitutional monarchy with the king as ceremonial head of state
A return to King Gyanendra's full executive powers
A referendum before any decision on the monarchy is made

questions.scenario: It's December 23, 1972, in the final seconds of the AFC divisional playoff at Three Rivers Stadium. Your Pittsburgh Steelers trail the Raiders, and Terry Bradshaw's desperation pass ricochets off a violent collision near midfield, bouncing toward you as running back Franco Harris.
questions.prompt: What do you do as the deflected ball drops toward your feet?
questions.butterflyEffect: Harris scooped the ball off his shoe tops and sprinted 42 yards for a touchdown, giving Pittsburgh a stunning 13-7 win forever known as the "Immaculate Reception." The play became a cornerstone of Steelers lore as the franchise launched into its 1970s dynasty, and its legality is still debated by fans to this day.

choices.text: Scoop the ball off your shoe tops and run it in for a touchdown
Let it fall to the ground, assuming it's incomplete
Signal for a fair catch to be safe
Spike the ball immediately to stop the clock

questions.scenario: You sit on Liberia's cabinet in October 1871. President Roye stands accused of secretly extending his own term and mishandling a controversial £100,000 loan raised in London, and outrage is spreading through Monrovia.
questions.prompt: What does the cabinet and legislature do about President Roye?
questions.butterflyEffect: Roye was deposed and arrested in what is remembered as modern Africa's first coup d'état; he drowned soon after while trying to flee Monrovia by sea. Vice President James Skivring Smith took over, and the episode set an early precedent for the removal of Liberian leaders by force that would echo in the country's later 20th-century coups.

choices.text: Depose him and place him under arrest
Ignore the allegations and let him finish his term
Call new elections while Roye stays in office
Send the matter to Liberia's supreme court for a slow review

questions.scenario: It is 26 October 1995 in Sliema, Malta. You are part of an Israeli Mossad team tracking Palestinian Islamic Jihad leader Fathi Shaqaqi, who has just checked into a hotel under a false identity while traveling from Libya.
questions.prompt: What does the Mossad team do to eliminate Shaqaqi?
questions.butterflyEffect: A motorcycle gunman shot Shaqaqi at close range outside the hotel, killing him instantly. Ramadan Shallah succeeded him as PIJ's leader, and the assassination fueled cycles of retaliatory violence between Israel and Palestinian militant groups in the years that followed.

choices.text: Shoot him at close range outside the hotel
Poison his food in the hotel restaurant
Plant a car bomb in the hotel parking lot
Abduct him and interrogate him in a safehouse

questions.scenario: You are a member of Congress on 26 October 2001, six weeks after the September 11 attacks. A sweeping anti-terrorism bill expanding surveillance and law enforcement powers is on your desk, and leadership wants a swift vote.
questions.prompt: What does Congress do with the USA PATRIOT Act?
questions.butterflyEffect: Congress passed the act by overwhelming margins and President Bush signed it into law that day, granting agencies broad new surveillance and detention powers. The law reshaped American security policy for over a decade, sparking recurring civil-liberties battles that culminated in the 2013 Snowden revelations and its eventual replacement by the USA Freedom Act.

choices.text: Pass it quickly with overwhelming bipartisan support
Vote it down over civil liberties concerns
Table it indefinitely for further study
Strip out all surveillance provisions before passing it

questions.scenario: You are an election official in South Vietnam in October 1955, tallying ballots from a referendum pitting Prime Minister Ngô Đình Diệm against former emperor Bảo Đại for control of the new state.
questions.prompt: What happens with the referendum results?
questions.butterflyEffect: Diệm's supporters reported a suspiciously lopsided victory, with turnout and margins that outstripped the eligible population in some districts. He proclaimed the Republic of Vietnam and became its first president, a rule that lasted until his assassination in the 1963 CIA-backed coup, deepening America's commitment to the war that followed.

choices.text: Diệm is declared the overwhelming winner amid fraud allegations
Bảo Đại narrowly wins and remains head of state
The vote is too close to call and a runoff is scheduled

questions.scenario: You are a factory delegate in Saint Petersburg in October 1905, as a general strike grips the city and workers gather to decide how to organize their growing movement.
questions.prompt: What do the assembled workers' delegates decide to create?
questions.butterflyEffect: They formed the Saint Petersburg Soviet of Workers' Deputies, a council that coordinated strikes and voiced demands directly to the authorities, with Leon Trotsky soon rising to prominence within it. Though the Tsarist government crushed it within weeks, the soviet became the model revived in 1917, when the Petrograd Soviet helped drive the Russian Revolution.

choices.text: A workers' council, or soviet, to coordinate the strike
A petition committee to appeal directly to the Tsar
An armed militia to seize government buildings immediately
A vote to end the strike and return to the factories

questions.scenario: It is 12 October 1799, high above Paris. You are Jeanne Geneviève Garnerin, alone in a hydrogen balloon at 900 metres, your husband's experimental parachute rigged beneath the basket, and the crowd below is waiting.
questions.prompt: What do you do to become the first woman to descend by parachute?
questions.butterflyEffect: She released the balloon and dropped beneath the canopy, landing safely and proving a woman could survive a parachute descent from altitude. Her feat, following her husband André-Jacques Garnerin's earlier jumps, helped establish parachuting as a serious pursuit rather than a mere circus stunt, inspiring generations of aeronauts and, eventually, military escape technology.

choices.text: Cut loose and jump, trusting the parachute to open beneath you
Refuse to jump and order the balloon brought down gently instead
Wait for your husband to jump first and follow only if he lands safely
Release gas from the balloon and float down still attached to the basket

questions.scenario: It is 12 October 1960 at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Filipino delegate Lorenzo Sumulong has just accused the Soviet Union of practicing colonialism in Eastern Europe, and Nikita Khrushchev, seated at the Soviet desk, is furious.
questions.prompt: What does Khrushchev reportedly do to register his outrage?
questions.butterflyEffect: According to widely repeated accounts, Khrushchev pulled off his shoe and pounded it on the desk in protest, though several eyewitnesses and later historians dispute whether this actually happened as described. True or exaggerated, the image became one of the defining, almost cartoonish symbols of Cold War brinkmanship and Khrushchev's combustible public style.

choices.text: He pulls off his shoe and pounds it on the desk
He storms out of the General Assembly hall
He demands the Filipino delegate be expelled from the UN
He calls for an immediate vote of censure against the Philippines

questions.scenario: It is 12 October 1960 in Tokyo, and you are in the studio audience for a live televised debate among party leaders. Suddenly a teenage ultranationalist bolts across the stage toward Japan Socialist Party leader Inejirō Asanuma.
questions.prompt: What does the attacker do as cameras keep rolling?
questions.butterflyEffect: Seventeen-year-old Otoya Yamaguchi stabbed Asanuma with a short sword, killing him live on air; Yamaguchi died in custody weeks later. Yasushi Nagao's photograph of the attack won a Pulitzer Prize and became one of the most famous news images of the twentieth century, and the killing deepened the era's bitter left-right political violence in Japan.

He shoots Asanuma with a pistol

questions.prompt: What do you do once you are standing on the floor of the House?
questions.butterflyEffect: Margaret Travers Symons shouted her demand before startled MPs could remove her, becoming the first woman to speak within the chamber of the House of Commons, though not as an elected member. The stunt drew fresh press attention to the suffragettes' direct-action tactics and became one of many escalating protests that pushed the campaign for women's votes further into the public eye.

Chain yourself to the nearest railing and wait to be arrested

questions.scenario: It is December 1972, and construction crews digging near Berlin's Lehrter Station uncover a skeleton believed to be Martin Bormann, Hitler's secretary who vanished amid the fall of Berlin in 1945.
questions.prompt: How should investigators confirm the skeleton's identity?
questions.butterflyEffect: Forensic odontologists compared the skull's teeth to dental records held by Bormann's former dentist, and in 1973 West German authorities declared the remains his, officially closing a decades-long manhunt. A 1998 DNA test on remains later cremated and scattered at sea confirmed the match beyond doubt.

questions.prompt: What should the responding officer do to end the standoff and stop further harm?

questions.butterflyEffect: The UCI stripped Armstrong of all seven Tour de France titles and banned him from cycling for life. The scandal became one of the biggest in sports history, prompting a broader reckoning with doping culture in professional cycling.

choices.text: Strip him of all seven titles and ban him for life

questions.scenario: You are in the audience at the Houston Grand Opera on October 22, 1987, watching the world premiere of a new opera that turns a sitting-era president's diplomatic trip to Beijing into grand, minimalist music theater.
questions.prompt: What becomes of this daring experiment in operatic subject matter?
questions.butterflyEffect: Nixon in China, composed by John Adams, went on to become one of the most frequently performed operas of the late 20th century, later staged by the Metropolitan Opera. Its success helped establish minimalism as a viable, mainstream operatic language.

choices.text: It becomes one of the most performed operas of its era

questions.scenario: You are the engine driver of an express train approaching Gare Montparnasse in Paris on 22 October 1895, running late, when you realize the train is coming into the terminus far too fast to stop at the buffers.
questions.prompt: What happens as the train fails to stop in time?
questions.butterflyEffect: The train smashed through the station's facade and toppled out onto the Place de Rennes below. choices.text: It crashes through the station wall and falls onto the square below
It derails safely inside the platform hall, causing only minor damage
The driver manages to stop it just short of the buffers
It collides head-on with another train inside the station

questions.butterflyEffect: Security forces killed all five Jaish-e-Mohammed gunmen before they could enter the main chamber, but nine security and staff personnel died in the fighting. India blamed Pakistan-based militant groups and massed a million troops on the border in Operation Parakram, bringing the two nuclear-armed nations to the brink of war for months.

choices.text: All five were killed by security forces before reaching lawmakers
They took several MPs hostage and negotiated their escape
They detonated explosives inside the main chamber
They fled the compound and were never identified

questions.prompt: What happened when wave after wave of Union troops charged the stone wall?
questions.butterflyEffect: Fourteen separate Union assaults were shattered by Confederate fire from the sunken road, producing over 12,000 Union casualties to the South's roughly 5,000. The catastrophic defeat shattered Union morale, led to Burnside's removal from command within weeks, and set the stage for his disastrous follow-up 'Mud March.'

choices.text: Repeated Union charges were repulsed with devastating losses
Union troops broke through and captured the heights
Confederate forces abandoned the wall and retreated south

questions.butterflyEffect: Foreigners including John Rabe established the Nanjing Safety Zone, sheltering roughly 200,000 civilians, though it could not stop the mass killing and atrocities that followed in the weeks after the city's capture. They negotiated a formal surrender that spared the population

A collision with another aircraft on the runway

A deliberate decision to fly through a hurricane

questions.butterflyEffect: Waller's men stormed the church, killing Colonel Bolle and capturing several hundred Royalist prisoners, a decisive Parliamentarian victory. The ban lasted until September 1994, lifted after the IRA ceasefire, and is now cited as a case study in the limits of censoring speech to fight terrorism.

choices.text: A worker mishandling a detonator with the wrong tool caused a spark

questions.butterflyEffect: The P-63 struck the B-17 during the pass, and both historic aircraft crashed, killing all six crew members aboard with no injuries on the ground. The NTSB investigation that followed led air show organizers to tighten separation and sequencing rules for formation flying by historic aircraft nationwide.

choices.text: The two aircraft collided in mid-air, destroying both and killing all aboard
The aircraft completed the pass safely and the show continued without incident
The B-17 made an emergency landing after an engine fire
The P-63 was grounded before the flight due to a mechanical fault

questions.scenario: It is November 1920 in Rapallo, and you are among the diplomats hammering out the border between the Kingdom of Italy and the newly formed Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes after the collapse of Austria-Hungary.
questions.prompt: What did the resulting Treaty of Rapallo grant to Italy?
questions.butterflyEffect: Italy secured Istria, Zadar, and several Adriatic islands, but the contested port of Fiume was left as an independent free state rather than annexed outright. The unresolved status of Fiume fed nationalist agitation, and Italy would seize it outright in 1924, deepening tensions with Yugoslavia that lingered into the Second World War.

Trieste, Ljubljana, and full control of Montenegro

questions.scenario: It is November 12, 2020, launch day for the PlayStation 5 in North America, Japan, and Australia. You've been refreshing retailer websites for weeks trying to secure a unit.
questions.prompt: What was the immediate reality for most buyers trying to get a PS5 at launch?
questions.butterflyEffect: A global semiconductor shortage combined with pandemic-driven demand and bot-driven scalpers left the PS5 in short supply for well over a year after launch. Sony's struggle to keep shelves stocked reshaped how retailers handled console drops, pushing many toward invite-only and lottery-style sales systems.

choices.text: Severe shortages meant most buyers couldn't find one in stores for months
Consoles were plentiful and prices were cut within weeks

questions.scenario: It is November 1932 in the Western Australian wheat belt. At the government's request, soldiers armed with Lewis machine guns have been sent to deal with tens of thousands of emus devastating farmers' crops.
questions.prompt: What was the outcome of this military operation against the emus?
questions.butterflyEffect: The so-called Emu War was a conspicuous failure: the emus proved fast, scattered, and hard to hit, and the operation was called off within weeks having killed only a small fraction of the birds. Farmers instead turned to bounty systems and exclusion fencing, and the episode became a famous, wry example of military force failing against wildlife.

choices.text: The operation largely failed and was withdrawn after killing relatively few emus
The soldiers wiped out the regional emu population within days
The emus were successfully herded into a new reserve

questions.scenario: It is November 12, 1912, on the Ross Ice Shelf. Your search party has trekked for days looking for Robert Falcon Scott's polar party, missing for eight months since their attempt on the South Pole.
questions.prompt: What did the search party find, and what did they do?
questions.butterflyEffect: They found a snow-covered tent containing the bodies of Scott, Wilson, and Bowers along with Scott's diaries and letters. Rather than attempt the impossible task of returning the bodies to Britain, they left them under a cairn of snow and ice, and the recovered diaries turned Scott's fatal failure into one of Britain's most enduring stories of heroism and sacrifice.

choices.text: They found the tent with the bodies and diaries, and left them under a cairn
They found the men alive but suffering from severe frostbite

questions.scenario: It's the evening of November 21, 1950. You are the telegraph operator at a remote junction near Valemount, British Columbia, tasked with relaying an order telling a westbound troop train to take the siding so an eastbound passenger train can pass safely on the single track.
questions.prompt: What must you do before letting the troop train proceed on the order?
questions.butterflyEffect: An operator's mishandled order meant the troop train never took the siding, and it collided head-on with the passenger train, killing 21 people, including 17 soldiers bound for the Korean War. The disaster and the manslaughter trial that followed raised early Canadian legal questions about individual blame versus systemic failure, and prompted tighter verification rules for train orders.

Pass the order along immediately without confirming it, to keep the schedule on time

questions.prompt: What happens when he throws the ball at the window?

questions.butterflyEffect: Carter reburied the top of the staircase to protect it and sent word to Lord Carnarvon in England, waiting nearly three weeks before Carnarvon arrived so they could open the tomb together. The eventual discovery of Tutankhamun's largely intact treasures triggered a worldwide craze for Egyptian art and design that reshaped 1920s fashion, architecture, and film.

choices.text: Reburied the staircase and waited for Lord Carnarvon to arrive from England
Broke the seal immediately and entered alone that night
Alerted the Egyptian government, which sealed off the site for years
Dynamited the doorway to speed up excavation

questions.scenario: It is 4 November 2016, and you are a UN climate official watching the Paris Agreement finally take legal force, more than a year after it was negotiated outside Paris.
questions.prompt: What condition had to be met before the agreement could enter into force?
questions.butterflyEffect: The treaty required ratification by at least 55 countries responsible for at least 55% of global greenhouse gas emissions, a threshold reached in October 2016 when the EU ratified. Barely a year later the newly elected U.S. president announced America's withdrawal, foreshadowing a pattern of U.S. exits and re-entries that would recur under later administrations.

choices.text: Ratification by 55 countries covering at least 55% of global emissions
Unanimous ratification by every UN member state
Approval by the five permanent UN Security Council members only
A binding vote in the U.S. Senate ratifying the treaty

questions.scenario: It is November 1970 in Los Angeles, and social workers have just found a 13-year-old girl who has spent most of her life confined and deprived of language. Linguists and psychologists quickly take an interest in her case.
questions.prompt: What scientific question did researchers hope her case would help answer?
questions.butterflyEffect: Researchers used her case to test the critical period hypothesis, the idea that language must be acquired before puberty or never fully mastered. She learned some vocabulary but never developed normal grammar, seeming to support the hypothesis, though later critics argued her prolonged abuse and shifting research team made the study scientifically and ethically flawed.

choices.text: Whether language could still be fully learned after the presumed critical period
Whether children could survive without any human contact at all
Whether isolation permanently damaged a child's eyesight
Whether feral children retained memories of animal caregivers

questions.prompt: What should the exposed revolutionaries do next?

Launch the uprising immediately that night
Surrender to the authorities and cooperate
Wait for reinforcements from revolutionaries in other provinces

Resign and plead no contest to one tax evasion charge

questions.scenario: It is 29 December 1928, and you serve as an aide to Zhang Xueliang, the young warlord ruling Manchuria after his father's assassination. Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist forces have swept north, and you must advise Zhang on his next move.
questions.prompt: What should Zhang Xueliang do about the Nationalist government in Nanjing?
questions.butterflyEffect: Zhang formally submitted, raising the Nationalist flag over Manchuria and nominally completing China's reunification under the Kuomintang. The uneasy alliance masked deep regional tensions that Japan would later exploit, seizing Manchuria in the 1931 Mukden Incident.

choices.text: Declare Manchuria's allegiance to the Nanjing government, raising its flag
Remain an independent warlord and resist Nationalist authority
Ally openly with Japan against the Nationalists

questions.prompt: What did the Senate do after Collor's resignation attempt?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Senate ruled his resignation did not end the trial, convicted him, and barred him from elected office for eight years. He was later acquitted on separate criminal charges, and the episode became a landmark in testing Brazil's young democratic institutions.

Accept the resignation and dismiss all charges

Call for new elections and drop the impeachment entirely

questions.prompt: What happened to Schumacher in the aftermath of the fall?
questions.butterflyEffect: He was airlifted to a Grenoble hospital and placed in a medically induced coma to treat severe brain trauma. He survived but never returned to public life, and the accident renewed global debate over off-piste skiing safety and helmet standards.

He was treated at the resort and skied again within days
He was flown to Paris for immediate surgery and returned to racing that season

questions.scenario: It is 29 December 1860 at Blackwall on the Thames. You watch as Britain's new warship, built to answer France's revolutionary ironclad Gloire, slides into the water for the first time.
questions.prompt: What did the launch of this new British ironclad mean for naval power?
questions.butterflyEffect: HMS Warrior, faster and more heavily armed than any ship afloat, instantly made existing wooden battlefleets obsolete and touched off an intense Anglo-French ironclad arms race. Within a generation, navies worldwide had abandoned wooden hulls entirely.

choices.text: It rendered existing wooden warships obsolete and escalated the ironclad arms race
It proved ironclads impractical and Britain returned to wooden ships

It ended naval competition between Britain and France entirely

questions.prompt: What should you do to stop the incendiary bombs from destroying the building?
questions.butterflyEffect: The raid gutted much of the historic City, destroying the Guildhall and eight Wren churches in a firestorm. It hardened Britain's civil defence doctrine around rooftop fire-watching and stirrup pumps, and stiffened public resolve through the ongoing Blitz.

Evacuate at once and wait for the professional fire brigade to arrive
Ignore small incendiaries since only high explosives matter
Remove all sand buckets to prevent looting during the raid

questions.scenario: It is 21 October 1805 off Cape Trafalgar. You stand on the deck of HMS Victory as Nelson's fleet of 27 ships closes on Villeneuve's 33 French and Spanish vessels. The traditional tactic is to sail parallel and trade broadsides, but Nelson has other plans.
questions.prompt: What order does Nelson give the British fleet as it approaches the enemy line?
questions.butterflyEffect: Nelson split his fleet into two columns and drove them perpendicular into the allied line, breaking it into isolated pockets that could be overwhelmed one by one.
